A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TwinMarket and contain readable methods, results, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original financial-market simulations, behavioral analyses, ablations, rumor experiments, and scalability results in Sections 4–7 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds component-level BDI ablation results in Appendix B.2.4.

M1.justification: The proposed full framework retains its BDI agents, persona initialization, social-network construction, post-ranking formula, trading mechanism, and prompts. The new formal description and experimental ablation variants do not establish a revision to the full method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Chinese A-share setting, SSE 50 and ten industry indices, Xueqiu/Guba transaction sources, news and announcements, and rumor scenarios. The new BDI ablation remains within this coverage; downstream synthetic-data applications are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v5 Table 9 introduces two evaluated comparison variants: TwinMarket w/o Belief Update and TwinMarket w/o Desire. The external ABM-HPM and ABM-BH comparisons in Table 4 and the previously evaluated ablation variants remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2.4 adds a June 15–July 15, 2023 evaluation with 100 GPT-4o agents, separately freezing beliefs and disabling proactive information queries. Existing experimental settings are retained; the added Table 5 explanation of metric inputs is documentation rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: v3 tests removal of the entire BDI framework; v5 additionally isolates belief updating and desire-driven information seeking in Appendix B.2.4. This supplies a limited component-level analysis while retaining the existing temperature, industry, social-interaction, network-sensitivity, and behavioral case analyses.

E5.justification: v3 Table 9 and v5 Table 10 both report three runs each for GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5-Flash using means and relative standard deviations. Existing significance and descriptive-statistics reporting is retained. The new ablation introduces no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v5 Table 9 adds RMSE/MAE pairs of 0.0158/0.0143 for Full BDI, 0.0342/0.0298 without belief updating, and 0.0532/0.0443 without desire. These are newly reported one-month results, not improvements over v3's longer-period evaluations. Existing main comparison and stability-table values are retained.

T1.justification: New Appendix E.2 introduces mathematical definitions for the five-dimensional belief state, belief/desire/intention mappings, and daily state-transition cycle. This is a limited formalization of the existing workflow; it adds no theorem or proof, and the existing financial and network equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal introductory contributions retain their scope. v5's conclusion additionally positions TwinMarket as a source of high-fidelity synthetic data for training and evaluating downstream models, including reinforcement-learning agents, extending its claimed contribution without evaluating that application.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly identifies the China A-share context, single daily call auction, and zero-sum environment as limitations. It also expands the information-aggregation interpretation of scaling and interprets the new ablations as evidence for the importance of adaptive beliefs and proactive information seeking.

D1.justification: v5 clarifies that Table 5 metrics use daily normalized index-price series, documents the BDI execution sequence, and updates the project-page link. It omits v3 Appendix G.2.3's explanation that engagement with propagated posts contributes to the original post's cumulative score.

R1.justification: v5 adds seven references, including work on financial LLMs, human-trust simulation, recommendation graphs, and automated research agents. Appendix A adds a connection to potentially self-improving simulation frameworks, while retaining the principal positioning against earlier ABMs and LLM simulations.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. v5 rewrites parts of Scalability and Conclusion, adds ethics and acknowledgment passages, relocates the impact statement and academic-use qualification, and updates affiliations and appendix organization.

P2.justification: v5 extensively redesigns the document with a boxed title/abstract, colored headings, highlighted stylized facts, restyled example and prompt panels, and widespread figure/table reflow. It merges the fundamental/technical examples, moves v3 Figure 29 into the main text as Figure 4, omits the old hot-score decay plot, and adds the granular-ablation table.

improvement.justification: The targeted BDI ablations add useful component-level evidence beyond v3's whole-BDI comparison, while metric clarification and explicit market/mechanics limitations improve assessability. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the post-propagation scoring explanation. The principal validation remains unchanged, and the new downstream synthetic-data claims are not empirically tested.
